newsitem.title: FRANCE: France welcomes resumed Israeli-Palestinian talks.
newsitem.headline: France welcomes resumed Israeli-Palestinian talks.

text.p: France welcomed Israeli-Palestinian agreement to resume peace talks after an emergency summit in Washington but said the two sides remained far apart.

President Jacques Chirac's office announced that Palestinian President Yasser Arafat would come to Paris to meet the French leader on Friday evening on his way home from the Washington summit, which achieved no concrete results.

"French authorities learned with interest of the statements made by (U.S.) President (Bill) Clinton on the results of the Washington talks" between Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Arafat, the Foreign Ministry said in a statement.
"There are still deep differences between the two sides but, as the U.S. president stressed, the thread of dialogue has been resumed," it said after the two-day summit on Wednesday.
"France welcomes the announcement of a resumption of Israeli-Palestinian talks at Erez" on the Israel-Gaza border from Sunday, it said. That agreement was the main outcome of the summit.

France "reaffirms its conviction that concrete measures must be taken to confirm the will of all sides to implement the agreements already in place", it said. France has criticised Israel for a flare-up of violence last week.
